memory_bridge: Under the meeting roof, first see the organization that owns it—会社 for On カイ—then watch two people actually meet and say 会う for Kun あう.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 会社（かいしゃ）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Hang the 会社（かいしゃ） company sign over the crowded meeting roof; its first character is read with On カイ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 会う（あう）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Two people enter from opposite sides, greet beneath the roof, and 会う（あう）—the full native verb fixes Kun あう, “to meet.”

memory_bridge: Use one road in three modes: 交通（こうつう） names traffic with On ツウ; a traveler 通る（とおる） through it, someone 通す（とおす） an object through it, and a commuter 通う（かよう） along it repeatedly.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 交通（こうつう）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Two streams meet on the same road as 交通（こうつう）—traffic. The common compound anchors On ツウ; English TWO lacks the initial affricate and is not a sufficiently close cue.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 通る（とおる）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: A traveler 通る（とおる） the gate—passes through under their own motion. This is the intransitive path.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 通す（とおす）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: The traveler 通す（とおす） a long pole through the gate—passes something through. This is the transitive partner.

anchors.gloss: to go to and from (a place)

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 通う（かよう）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Footprints cover the same road there and back each day as the traveler 通う（かよう）—commutes or goes regularly.
readings.usage_gloss: to go to and from (a place)
